name: @12-apps/backend-harness
description: Consumer harness for the server-side packages, built against the PUBLISHED tarballs. scripts/harness-install.mjs turns this into package.json by adding the @12-apps dependencies as file: tarballs.
//s3: @aws-sdk/client-s3 is @12-apps/storage's OPTIONAL peer (12-20), installed here on purpose: it is what a consumer that wants a bucket installs, and the only way `@12-apps/storage/s3` can be proven to resolve from the tarball. It arrived transitively via shared-helpers before, which is not a promise anything holds.
//server: No longer tests-only: `src/` is a REAL server, mounting the package's own Hono router over a real PGlite, so the SPA's Save leaves the tab and survives a reload. `tsx` runs the TypeScript directly — the harness has no build step and should not grow one, because a `dist/` between the source and the server is one more thing that can explain a failure that is supposed to be about OUR packages.
//realtime: ws + @types/ws are here because @12-apps/realtime/gateway declares ws as an OPTIONAL peer and only that entry imports it. tests/realtime-gateway.test.ts starts the published gateway and connects a real socket to it, which is the only way to prove the runnable entry is genuinely runnable from a tarball.
//notifications: web-push is here for the same reason: @12-apps/notifications/web-push declares it as an OPTIONAL peer and only that entry imports it, so a host that never enables the channel never installs it. tests/notifications-entry-points.test.ts builds a real VAPID signer out of the tarball, which is what proves that subpath resolves at all.
//prisma: prisma + @prisma/client + pglite-prisma-adapter are pinned EXACTLY, and to the same versions packages/prisma uses. Prisma's generated client and its CLI are one artifact split across two packages, and a range would let npm resolve them apart on a lockfile-less install — which fails as a generated client the runtime refuses rather than as an install error. pglite-prisma-adapter is what makes a REAL PrismaClient run over the same in-process PGlite the SQL seams use; see src/prisma.ts for why the harness wants both.
